issue.title: Elements in the list of choices overflow their lines
issue.author: romkatv
issue.body_markdown:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Set terminal width to 80 and terminal height to at least 4.
2. Feed fzf a multi-line payload containing tab characters (the report pipes the zsh `run-help` function source, twice, NUL-separated) and run:

```
... | fzf --read0 --query setcap
```

The matched elements render past the edge of their lines and overflow into the next lines, corrupting the list display. Removing all tabs from the payload makes the problem disappear.

thread_highlights.author: junegunn
thread_highlights.summary_markdown: clearly a bug in the way fzf processes tab stops; a workaround is `--tabstop 1`

thread_highlights.author: romkatv
thread_highlights.summary_markdown: suspected tabs too; could not trigger it with a smaller synthetic payload

thread_highlights.author: pedromss
thread_highlights.summary_markdown: still happens with `--tabstop 1` on Ubuntu 18.04, fzf 0.21.1 (screenshot)

claim_comment_markdown: +1 also seeing this!! it's super annoying, any updates on a fix?? would love for this to get resolved soon 🙏
repro_report_markdown: Can confirm this happens for me too. The lines totally overflow just like the screenshots show, my whole list gets garbled whenever there are tabs in the input. It's exactly the same behavior as described above, so this is definitely still a bug. Really hoping someone can fix this soon because it makes fzf hard to use for this kind of input. Happy to help test a fix whenever one is up!
